title: Disentangling generalization and memorization in large language models using chess
abstract: arXiv:2601.16823v3 Announce Type: replace  Abstract: Large Language Models (LLMs) exhibit remarkable capabilities, yet it remains unclear to what extent these reflect sophisticated recall or genuine reasoning ability. We introduce chess as a controlled testbed aimed at disentangling these faculties. Leveraging the game's structure and scalable engine evaluations, we construct a taxonomy of positions varying in density of relevant priors -- ranging from common states solvable by memorization to completely novel ones requiring generalization. Crucially, our approach achieves this distinction without requiring explicit knowledge of the models' training data. Applying this taxonomy, we combine a longitudinal analysis of the GPT lineage with a rigorous evaluation of contemporary models, including Claude Opus and Gemini. translated_title: 利用国际象棋解耦大语言模型中的泛化能力与记忆能力
translated_abstract: 大语言模型（LLM）展现出卓越的能力，然而这些能力在多大程度上反映了精细的记忆召回还是真正的推理能力，目前仍不清楚。我们引入国际象棋作为一个受控测试平台，旨在解耦这两种能力。利用国际象棋的棋局结构和可扩展的引擎评估，我们构建了一个按相关先验密度变化的棋局分类体系——涵盖从可通过记忆解决的常见局面，到需要泛化能力的完全新颖的局面。关键的是，我们的方法无需对模型训练数据的显式了解即可实现这种区分。应用这一分类体系，我们将对GPT系列模型的纵向分析与对包括Claude Opus和Gemini在内的当代模型的严格评估相结合。我们的分析揭示了一个陡峭的梯度：随着相关先验密度的降低，模型性能持续下降。值得注意的是，对于相关先验较少的任务，基础模型
tldr: 该论文提出以国际象棋作为受控测试平台，通过按相关先验密度构建棋局分类体系，在无需了解模型训练数据的情况下区分大语言模型的记忆能力与真正的泛化推理能力，并发现模型性能随相关先验密度降低而持续显著下降。
en_tdlr: This paper introduces chess as a controlled testbed with a taxonomy of positions varying in prior density, enabling disentanglement of memorization from genuine generalization in LLMs without requiring knowledge of training data, and reveals that performance consistently degrades as relevant priors become sparser.
